<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` now runs MXFP4 MoE checkpoints, such as DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, on Hopper. It uses FlashInfer's SM90 MXFP4 x FP8 MegaMoE (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4843) through the existing FlashInfer MoE-EP adapter. The packed MXFP4 weights go to the kernel as loaded, without a bf16 round trip.

- **Stacked on #62603** (SM90 block-FP8 MegaMoE through the same adapter). Only the last commit, db751d56eb, is new here.
- **Draft until FlashInfer ships [#4843](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4843) in a release.** It is not in 0.7.2.post1, main's current pin.
- This answers the question in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62603#issuecomment-6460588074: it is an MXFP4-resident Hopper moe_ep entry, and it applies to an unmodified DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint.

Related:
- #64061: the same goal through DeepGEMM's SM90 FP8 x FP4 Mega MoE (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#44). It is measured head to head below. The two kernels trade wins: DeepGEMM is faster in decode and this PR is faster in prefill.
- #54032: FlashInfer's CUTLASS Humming grouped-GEMM MoE for the same quantization. It is not a megakernel.

## Claims

All results are DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8x H200, compared against main's default MXFP4 backend (HUMMING with block-FP8 activations and `allgather_reducescatter`):

- **Decode** (DP8/EP8, 128K/512, DSpark3 with synthetic acceptance): +8% to +18% output throughput and -6% to -13% TPOT p50 at concurrency 32 to 192. No resolved change at concurrency 8.
- **Prefill** (DP4/EP4 at the full 1M context, 2048/1, natural DSpark3): +3.5% saturated throughput and lower TTFT p50 at every offered rate.
- **#64061**, on the same workload: +12% to +21% in decode, but -8.7% in prefill.
- **GSM8K** shows no resolved difference among the three backends.
- The backend is opt-in. Default backends do not change.

## Validation

**Setup.**
- vLLM main 77f58e5304, on the native build of the 1cb31be702 nightly wheel. Between those two commits, csrc, cmake, setup and requirements are identical.
- All arms use FlashInfer nightly 0.7.2.dev20261027, torch 2.14.0+cu130, and DeepGEMM#44 at f4685f201e.
- Arms:
  - main: default backend.
  - main + #64061 (335cff32bf): `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`.
  - main + #62603 + this PR: `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`.
  - The trees differ only in each PR's files. The FlashInfer arm's 12 files hash-match this branch.
- Order is serial on the same GPUs: main A1, #64061, this PR, main A2. "main" is the mean of the A1 and A2 medians.
- Client: `vllm-rs bench serve` with token-ID prompts.

**Decode.** DP8/EP8, DecodeBenchConnector, ISL 128K / OSL 512, DSpark with 3 draft tokens and synthetic acceptance [0.8, 0.6, 0.5], N = 2C prompts. Each arm runs a warm-up pass, then three passes; cells are three-pass medians.

| C | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 192 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| output tok/s, main | 1338 | 3641 | 5806 | 8823 | 10130 |
| output tok/s, #64061 | 1507 (+12.6%) | 4336 (+19.1%) | 6986 (+20.3%) | 9879 (+12.0%) | 12237 (+20.8%) |
| output tok/s, this PR | 1371 (+2.4%) | 3950 (+8.5%) | 6425 (+10.7%) | 9575 (+8.5%) | 11981 (+18.3%) |
| TPOT p50 ms, main | 5.00 | 7.03 | 8.35 | 9.58 | 12.05 |
| TPOT p50 ms, #64061 | 4.37 | 5.50 | 6.58 | 8.35 | 9.04 |
| TPOT p50 ms, this PR | 4.96 | 6.50 | 7.61 | 9.02 | 10.48 |

The two main arms differ by -5.8% at C=8 and by at most 3.3% elsewhere. The +2.4% at C=8 is inside that spread.

![Decode: output throughput and TPOT p50 by concurrency for main, #64061 and this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qianlihuang/vllm/c850c6b27d4b8273b429434f6e5350aa4fa8100c/decode-comparison.png)

<details>
<summary>Decode output tok/s, median [min, max] of the three passes per arm</summary>

| C | main A1 | #64061 | this PR | main A2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 1378 [1346, 1420] | 1507 [1473, 1570] | 1371 [1345, 1425] | 1298 [1253, 1316] |
| 32 | 3702 [3700, 3735] | 4336 [4326, 4397] | 3949 [3879, 4004] | 3580 [3571, 3584] |
| 64 | 5763 [5721, 5855] | 6986 [6940, 6987] | 6425 [6318, 6501] | 5850 [5751, 5895] |
| 128 | 8894 [8850, 8972] | 9879 [9524, 9908] | 9575 [9528, 9657] | 8751 [7969, 8888] |
| 192 | 10220 [10214, 10242] | 12237 [12130, 12241] | 11981 [11912, 12171] | 10040 [9883, 10309] |

</details>

**Prefill.**
- DP4/EP4 on 4x H200 at the default (full, 1M) context length, ISL 2048 / OSL 1, natural DSpark3.
- Saturation: 64 warm-up requests, then 3 x 1000 requests at an unlimited rate.
- Poisson sweep: 60 s of load at each rate, at 0.5 to 1.1 times main A1's saturation.

| | main (A1 / A2) | #64061 | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| saturated req/s, three runs | 40.47 / 40.68 / 40.47; 40.21 / 40.54 / 40.30 | 36.44 / 36.89 / 36.90 | 41.80 / 41.84 / 41.81 |
| saturated req/s vs main | 40.39 | 36.89 (-8.7%) | 41.81 (+3.5%) |
| TTFT p50 ms at 20.2 / 32.4 / 40.5 / 44.5 req/s | 569 / 802 / 1166 / 4553 | 600 / 943 / 2635 / 7684 | 521 / 778 / 1072 / 3539 |
| TTFT p99 ms at the same rates | 1080 / 1201 / 2249 / 6037 | 1126 / 1336 / 6053 / 12693 | 1009 / 1189 / 1821 / 4334 |

At 44.5 req/s, main serves 40.5 req/s, #64061 serves 36.7 req/s and this PR serves 41.7 req/s.

![Prefill: TTFT p50 and p99 by offered request rate for main, #64061 and this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qianlihuang/vllm/c850c6b27d4b8273b429434f6e5350aa4fa8100c/prefill-comparison.png)

**GSM8K.** 1319 questions, 5-shot, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` against the prefill servers with natural DSpark3.

| main A1 | main A2 | #64061 | this PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 89.8% | 90.5% | 90.4%, 89.9% | 90.4%, 91.1% |

One standard error is about 0.8 points, so no difference is resolved.

**Tests.** On H200 with FlashInfer 0.7.2.dev20261027:

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py   # 23 passed
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py   # CPU: 9 passed
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k sm90_init_warmup
# SM90 GPU: 16 passed (MXFP4 and block FP8, 4 expert shapes x EP2/EP4)
```

- The SM90 GPU test is exact on grid inputs. It covers the GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Kimi-K3 and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next expert shapes.
- For MXFP4 it runs with DeepSeek-V4 routing, which exercises the output view, the workspaces, an idle rank and a CUDA graph replay.
- CI does not run the GPU cases. They need at least two Hopper GPUs, `nvshmem4py`, and a FlashInfer build with [#4843](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4843); without one they skip.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

Every server runs with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. The main arm omits `--moe-backend`; the #64061 arm passes `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`.

The loader is `safetensors` with prefetch for all arms. `fastsafetensors` OOMs here: it allocates a 94.6 GiB transient device buffer on top of 51.8 GiB of parameters.

```bash
# Decode
vllm serve <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash> --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0}' \
  --load-format safetensors --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"DecodeBenchConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_rates":[0.8,0.6,0.5]}' \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl

vllm-rs bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 512 \
  --prompt-token-ids --ignore-eos --request-rate inf --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $((2 * C)) --seed 0

# Prefill
vllm serve <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash> --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0}' \
  --load-format safetensors --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl

# warm-up: --num-prompts 64 --seed 100; saturation: --seed 102, 104, 106
vllm-rs bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 1 \
  --prompt-token-ids --ignore-eos --request-rate inf --num-prompts 1000 --seed 102
# Poisson: R in 20.2 28.3 32.4 36.4 40.5 44.5, N = round(60 * R), seeds 200 to 205
vllm-rs bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 1 \
  --prompt-token-ids --ignore-eos --request-rate $R --num-prompts $N --seed $SEED

# GSM8K, on each prefill server
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port $PORT
```
</details>

## Details

- **Weights.**
  - The MXFP4 oracle keeps the checkpoint's packed E2M1 bytes and E8M0 scales on Hopper. The adapter hands them to FlashInfer as `PrequantizedMoEWeights`.
  - FlashInfer interleaves gate/up rows and folds the scales into its kernel layout, an 11-exponent window per expert; it does not requantize.
  - On Blackwell nothing changes: the CuTeDSL kernel still gets bf16 and requantizes to NVFP4.
- **Activations.**
  - The kernel quantizes activations to E4M3 with one scale per token, and its fc2 input with one scale per 64 channels.
  - main's default uses block-FP8 (1x128) activations, so the arms are not bit-identical. GSM8K shows no resolved difference.
- **Adapter.**
  - `FlashInferMoeEp` takes the Hopper weight format (`"fp8_block"` or `"mxfp4"`) instead of a block-FP8 flag.
  - The MXFP4 path reuses #62603's 64/256/1024-token workspaces. With DeepSeek-V4 routing they now combine with FlashInfer's output view.
  - The kernel requires int64 expert ids, so the adapter converts top-k ids to the kernel's index dtype. This is one device-side cast per layer; nothing new reads back to the host.
- **Limitations.**
  - EPLB is rejected for MXFP4 on Hopper, because FlashInfer keeps a per-expert FP32 scale of these weights outside the layer's parameters.
  - Input-side router weights are rejected, as for block FP8: the kernel weights the activation before fc2.
  - The DeepGEMM MoE-EP backend stays Blackwell-only.
  - With a FlashInfer that lacks [#4843](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4843), MXFP4 on Hopper fails at weight processing with a message that names the FlashInfer PR.
- **Versus #64061.** DeepGEMM's kernel is faster in decode at every tested concurrency; the gap is 2% to 10%, smallest at C=192. This kernel is faster in prefill (41.8 vs 36.9 saturated req/s). The two can coexist as backend choices, for example per prefill/decode role.

  - The MXFP4 path reuses #62603's 64/256/1024-token workspaces. With DeepSeek-V4 routing they now combine with FlashInfer's output view.
  - The kernel requires int64 expert ids, so the adapter converts top-k ids to the kernel's index dtype. This is one device-side cast per layer; nothing new reads back to the host.
- **Limitations.**
  - EPLB is rejected for MXFP4 on Hopper, because FlashInfer keeps a per-expert FP32 scale of these weights outside the layer's parameters.
  - Input-side router weights are rejected, as for block FP8: the kernel weights the activation before fc2.
  - The DeepGEMM MoE-EP backend stays Blackwell-only.
  - With a FlashInfer that lacks [#4843](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4843), MXFP4 on Hopper fails at weight processing with a message that names the FlashInfer PR.
- **Versus #64061.** DeepGEMM's kernel is faster in decode at every tested concurrency; the gap is 2% to 10%, smallest at C=192. This kernel is faster in prefill (41.8 vs 36.9 saturated req/s). The two can coexist as backend choices, for example per prefill/decode role.

+def _block_fp8(weight: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Block FP8 with power-of-two scales: exact for the grid weights."""
+    experts, rows, cols = weight.shape
+    blocks = weight.float().view(experts, rows // 128, 128, cols // 128, 128)
+    absmax = blocks.abs().amax(dim=(2, 4))
+    scale = torch.where(
+        absmax > 0,
+        torch.exp2(torch.ceil(torch.log2(absmax / 448.0))),
+        torch.ones_like(absmax),
+    )

+def _quantize_block_fp8(real: torch.Tensor, power_of_two: bool):
+    *lead, rows, cols = real.shape
+    blocks = real.reshape(*lead, rows // 128, 128, cols // 128, 128)
+    scale = blocks.abs().amax(dim=(-3, -1)) / 448.0
+    if power_of_two:
+        scale = torch.exp2(torch.ceil(torch.log2(scale)))
+    return (real / _per_element(scale)).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn), scale
+
+
+def _per_element(scale: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return scale.repeat_interleave(128, -2).repeat_interleave(128, -1)
+
+
+def _gate_up_interleaved(w13: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Rows ordered [pair, {gate, up}, 8], the SM90 megakernel's FC1 layout."""
+    experts, rows, cols = w13.shape
+    gate, up = w13.view(experts, 2, rows // 16, 8, cols).unbind(1)
+    return torch.stack((gate, up), dim=2).reshape(experts, rows, cols)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("power_of_two", [True, False])
+def test_sm90_fp8_block_weights_keep_checkpoint_values(power_of_two: bool):
+    """Interleaving gate and up rows puts two checkpoint blocks under one scale.
+
+    Power-of-two scales survive that up to rounding below the E4M3 normal
+    range; other scales round the rescaled half once.
+    """
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    real = torch.randn(2, 512, 256) * 0.02
+    # Gate blocks 8x the up blocks, so each interleaved block mixes scales.
+    real[:, :256] *= 8.0
+    w13, scale = _quantize_block_fp8(real, power_of_two)
+
+    kernel_w13, kernel_scale = sm90_fp8_block_moe_ep_weights(w13, scale)
+
+    assert kernel_w13.dtype == w13.dtype and kernel_w13.shape == w13.shape
+    assert kernel_scale.shape == scale.shape
+    restored = kernel_w13.float() * _per_element(kernel_scale)
+    expected = _gate_up_interleaved(w13.float() * _per_element(scale))
+    error = (restored - expected).abs()
+    if power_of_two:
+        # Half the smallest E4M3 subnormal step.
+        assert torch.all(error <= 2.0**-10 * _per_element(kernel_scale))
+    else:
+        assert (error.norm() / expected.norm()).item() < 0.03

+    w13: torch.Tensor,

+    """Reorder block-FP8 ``w13`` (gate rows, then up rows) for the SM90 kernel.
+
+    After the gate/up interleave a 128-row scale block holds 64 gate and 64 up
+    rows from two checkpoint blocks. Both take the larger of the two scales and
+    the other half is rescaled. Power-of-two scales make that an exponent
+    shift, so only values that drop out of the E4M3 normal range round.
+
+    Args:
+        w13: ``(E, 2 * I, H)`` E4M3 weights.
+        w13_scale: ``(E, 2 * I / 128, H / 128)`` float32 dequantization scales.
+
+    Returns:

+        ``(E, 2 * I / 128, H / 128)`` scales.
+

+    intermediate = two_i // 2
+    num_blocks = intermediate // _FP8_BLOCK
+    assert intermediate % _FP8_BLOCK == 0 and hidden % _FP8_BLOCK == 0, w13.shape
+    assert w13_scale.shape == (num_experts, 2 * num_blocks, hidden // _FP8_BLOCK)
